headline: Crude Oil Holds Gains Following Saudi Attacks and Supply Concerns
summary: Crude oil prices sustained recent gains after attacks in Saudi Arabia heightened supply risks, despite Strait of Hormuz export volumes returning to normal.
why: Saudi Arabia holds a key position in global crude supply, making Middle Eastern infrastructure security crucial for oil price benchmarks.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Threats to Saudi energy facilities elevate geopolitical risk premiums in global oil trading.

why_moved: Oil prices held gains as news of Saudi attacks outweighed reports of normalized transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
